title: 1954 AHSME Problem 2
statement: The equation \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{2x^2}{x-1}-\frac{2x+7}{3} &{}+\frac{4-6x}{x-1}\\ &{}+1=0 \end{aligned} \] can be transformed by eliminating fractions to the equation \(x^2-5x+4=0.\) The roots of the latter equation are \(4\) and \(1.\) Then the roots of the first equation are:

solutions.text:
The transformed quadratic factors as \((x-1)(x-4)=0.\) However, the original equation has denominator \(x-1,\) so it is undefined at \(x=1.\) Substitution of \(x=4\) is valid and satisfies the original equation.

Thus, the only root is \(4,\) and the correct answer is C.
hints: Check both roots against the denominator in the original equation
Clearing a denominator can introduce a value at which the original expression is undefined
